headline: Embolo's dismissal; Argentina's delayed breakthrough
story: Argentina controlled possession from the start (55%), scoring in the 10th minute. Switzerland pressed relentlessly with 7.1 high-press phases, keeping Argentina at bay despite their possession advantage. The match turned decisively at 72 minutes when Breel Embolo's red card dismantled Switzerland's aggressive setup. Messi and Mac Allister (8.2 and 8.3 ratings) maintained Argentina's rhythm thereafter, though the expected avalanche never materialised.

Argentina's xG of 1.99 masked imprecision: they squandered a clear chance (0.38 xG) at 89 minutes that should have ended it. Switzerland's 0.44 xG reflected offensive poverty despite their aggressive press—their pressing suffocated by Embolo's absence in extra time. Messi and Lautaro Martinez (8.2, 8.0) drove Argentina through, converting low-xG chances (0.03, 0.28) to seal it. Ball recovery times favoured Argentina (15.3s vs 19.4s); they outlasted a team reduced to ten.

keyMoment.text: Embolo's dismissal removed Switzerland's pressing anchor; ten-man football ahead of extra time proved untenable.

home.verdict: Midfield control (Mac Allister 8.3, Messi 8.2) won it; survived the 89-minute miss that should have finished it sooner.
points: 55% possession and 22 shots established superiority Argentina never relinquished despite Switzerland's aggressive press.
Ball recovery advantage (15.3s vs 19.4s) allowed Argentina to control tempo; faster refreshes won the attritional extra time.
Extra-time finishes at 0.03 and 0.28 xG seem fortunate until you recall Argentina created 1.99 xG overall.

away.verdict: A clinical finisher would have exploited their 43 forced turnovers and 7.1 high-press phases; 0.44 xG was fatal.
points: 7.1 high-press phases and 43 forced turnovers created openings—but without a No. 9 to finish, they came to nothing.
Embolo's dismissal at 72 came right after their 67-minute equalizer; ten-man football in extra time was unrecoverable.
Dan Ndoye's 7.5 rating—their leading outfield performer—could not match Messi (8.2) and Mac Allister (8.3) alone.

statLine: Switzerland forced 43 turnovers and pressed 7.1 times but created just 0.44 xG—a masterclass in defensive intensity without attacking reward.
